newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Spanish strike disrupts car output in Portugal.
newsitem.headline: Spanish strike disrupts car output in Portugal.

text.p: A 13-day-old strike by Spanish truck drivers disrupted production at car assembly plants across Portugal on Tuesday, officials said.

Celia Roque, spokeswoman at a factory in Setubal south of Lisbon that assembles Renault Clio saloons, said production was halted on Tuesday and would not resume until Thursday because of insufficient deliveries of parts from Spain.
She said supplies ranging from engines to brakes and door panels had been delayed.
Spokesman Ricardo Oliveira said production at a Renault plant at Cacia, south of the city of Aveiro in central Portugal, was continuing on Tuesday.
"Some truck deliveries were delayed. Production is assured until tomorrow. Everything depends on the flow of trucks," he told Reuters.

A source at Portugal's biggest car manufacturer, the Ford-Volkswagwen AutoEuropa joint venture, said the plant had cut production on Monday and Tuesday because of delays in the delivery of parts from Spain.
Production of passenger vans had been cut to between 415 and 420 on Monday at the plant at Palmela, 50 km (30 miles) south of Lisbon, from 480 normally.
Production at the Ford plant at Azambuja, 30 km (19 miles) north of Lisbon, was halted on Friday and Monday. Like the AutoEuropa plant, it does not operate at the weekend.
Spokesman Artur Lemos told Reuters he expected the Ford plant to assemble pickup trucks on Tuesday but said: "I cannot guarantee that production will be 100 percent".
Opel, a unit of U.S. carmaker General Motors Corp, cut production at its Azambuja factory, which normally assembles 240 vans per day, to 70 percent capacity on Tuesday.
"We are reviewing the situation hourly," spokesman Miguel Tome told Reuters. "We were forced to interrupt some lines at the factory."

Stocks at French carmaker Citroen, which produces Saxo saloons in Mangualde near the city of Viseu in northern Portugal, had diminished because of the strike, but production was continuing on Tuesday, a company source said.
